extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.publisher: IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Independent, Camegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The questions were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials. Annotators collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning were performed: 1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. 2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. 3) Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels, and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators (over 50 university students) collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions where necessary. They adhered to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting redistribution. They selected questions without immediately available answers to avoid data contamination. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects; 90 college senior students (3 student experts per subject) for human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Version Change Log exists (V1 to V4). A live-updating leaderboard is available.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None (Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Expert AGI could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. It is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI as there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing, Evaluation of multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.
